mutation: goal: replace 'block the cell the runner is heading toward' (reactive pursuit) with a maximize-containment objective over a scheduled, budget-limited blocking policy that must pre-seal fixed gates before a faster runner's known-in-advance arrival time; input: sparse named gates on an otherwise walled border force explicit escape-route counting instead of a uniform perimeter.
theme: Trapping something that moves faster than you
title: Sparse Gates: Sealing a Faster Runner's Only Exits
strategies: trivial: do nothing (empty blocking policy every turn)
greedy: reactive chase -- every turn, spend the per-turn budget on cells immediately adjacent to the runner's CURRENT position, in the direction of whichever gate looks nearest right now

strong: predictive gate scheduler -- rank all gates by initial distance / build time, and dedicate budget turn by turn to fully sealing the most urgent still-open gate before the runner can arrive, exploiting that gate locations and arrival times are computable from turn 1
invalid: places a block on the runner's own starting cell -- must be rejected (score 0)
